title: How Many Credentials Should Your AI Agent Have? Zero. — Jim Clark, Docker
talk_summary: Docker's Jim Clark argues agents should run in task-scoped sandboxes with zero credentials, routing all MCP traffic through a gateway that controls which tools, resources, and network access each sandbox gets. Capabilities are progressively disclosed per task intent, and identity is exchanged via OAuth/ID-JAG so credentials never live inside the agent.

takeaways.what_they_do: Every harness points at a single internal MCP gateway endpoint; the gateway injects credentials and controls which tools/resources each sandbox can reach, so no secrets sit inside the agent environment.
takeaways.evidence_quote: how many credentials should be in uh a sandbox. Well, I mean the the the right answer is always zero.

takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of configuring MCPs separately per harness (Codex, Claude Code, etc.), one gateway endpoint serves all harnesses, making the harness a swappable parameter of the sandbox.
takeaways.evidence_quote: suddenly all your harnesses are MCP agnostic... you almost make the harness a parameter of the sandbox.

takeaways.technique: Progressive disclosure of tools per task
takeaways.what_they_do: Only expose the MCPs/tools a given task needs, not all 50 a workflow might use, keeping context small and each sandbox matching task intent.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Just because you might at some point in a workflow use 50 different MCPs, doesn't mean that each sandbox has to have all 50 of those MCPs.

takeaways.what_they_do: Split researcher, fact-checker, and publisher into separate sandboxes with different network/tool access so no single agent both ingests untrusted context and holds write tools.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we break it up into logical sandboxes, so at each individual point, we have a don't have a dangerous concept a dangerous combination

takeaways.what_they_do: Model the sandbox on the intent of the current step (e.g., git signing keys only present during the ~2 min commit window, not the whole hour-long run).
takeaways.evidence_quote: In an hour, it might be it might need, say, my my my Git signing keys for like 2 minutes of that time.
takeaways.numbers: ~2 minutes of an hour-long run needs signing keys

takeaways.technique: Identity exchange (ID-JAG) instead of stored creds
takeaways.what_they_do: Gateway exchanges agent identity claims with the existing IdP to get a scoped authorization grant for downstream resource servers, avoiding consent screens and stored secrets.
takeaways.evidence_quote: by exchanging identity claims with your identity provider... you can get back a new thing... called an ID jag, an authorization grant.
